desc: Build the global integration analysis prompt context for a frozen contributing set with fewer than two scopes, which by design persists no coverage records.
done_when: `populateGlobalIntegrationContext` in `internal/agent/prompt.go` returns nil and produces an empty `RoleContextData.IntegrationCoverage` when `goal.integration.contributing_set` holds zero or one scope and `goal.integration.coverage` is empty, so both the integration-analyst and integration-reviewer role contexts render for that state. It still fails when a contributing set of two or more scopes is missing coverage for any scope, still fails when a coverage record names a plan outside the frozen contributing set, and still validates every coverage payload it does render. A new case in `internal/agent/prompt_integration_test.go` renders analyst and reviewer context for a one-scope cohort with empty coverage and for a zero-scope cohort, asserts both succeed and contain the GLOBAL INTEGRATION CONTEXT heading, and fails against the pre-fix implementation with the current `lacks coverage for plan` error.
scope: Own `internal/agent/prompt.go` and `internal/agent/prompt_integration_test.go`. The global branch of `internal/prompts/templates/blocks/branch_integration_context.tmpl` may be touched only to make the empty-coverage wording accurate for a bypassed single-scope cohort. Do not change `internal/ops/integration_progress.go`, `internal/ops/integration_reconcile.go`, the persisted coverage model, or the two-or-more-scope coverage requirement.

desc: Resolve live integration HEAD through one shared helper so every sliced-integration consumer compares the same ref resolution.
done_when: One shared helper owns integration-HEAD resolution for the integration lifecycle, and `internal/ops/integration_reconcile.go`, `internal/ops/pipeline_ops.go`, `internal/ops/integration_mutation_lock.go`, `internal/prompts/wake.go`, and `internal/agent/workdetection.go` all obtain integration HEAD from it, with one explicit ref form and one documented empty-branch policy instead of today's mix of `GetCommitSHA(state.Config.IntegrationBranch)` and `GetCommitSHA("refs/heads/" + branch)` plus an unreachable `"" -> "main"` fallback. A new test creates a repository whose integration branch name is also a tag pointing at a different commit, and asserts the helper resolves the branch commit and that a reconciled global analysis `source_commit` equals the commit that `verifyCleanIntegrationSource` compares against; the test fails against the pre-fix implementation. Existing `internal/ops`, `internal/prompts`, `internal/agent`, and `internal/integration` tests stay green.
scope: Own the new shared HEAD-resolution helper and its call sites in `internal/ops/integration_reconcile.go`, `internal/ops/pipeline_ops.go`, `internal/ops/integration_mutation_lock.go`, `internal/prompts/wake.go`, `internal/agent/workdetection.go`, plus the tests covering them. Preserve the existing completion -> mutation -> blackboard-read lock order and every current call-site behaviour other than ref resolution. Do not change the evidence model, the progress decision, or unrelated `GetCommitSHA` callers outside the integration lifecycle.

desc: Give live integration progress evaluation one shared owner across prompt rendering and agent work detection.
done_when: Exactly one shared live evaluator loads the frozen pipeline capability, resolves integration HEAD through the helper introduced by output[1], calls `EvaluateIntegrationProgress`, and returns the decision or evaluation error. Both `internal/prompts/builder.go` and `internal/agent/workdetection.go` obtain those inputs from it and pass them to the existing pure `ProjectEffectiveIntegrationCompletion` mapping; `evaluateEffectiveIntegrationWakeProjection` and the second frozen-pipeline/HEAD/evaluation copy are gone. The live evaluator is owned at the narrowest existing dependency-safe boundary rather than being required to live in `internal/prompts`. Focused behavior cases in `internal/prompts/builder_test.go` and `internal/agent/workdetection_test.go` prove both consumers retain the same complete, waiting, blocked, exhausted, unavailable, and reconciliation-needed wake outcomes.
scope: Own `internal/agent/workdetection.go`, `internal/agent/workdetection_test.go`, `internal/prompts/wake.go`, `internal/prompts/builder.go`, `internal/prompts/builder_test.go`, and, only if it is the dependency-safe live-evaluation owner, `internal/ops/integration_progress.go` plus `internal/ops/integration_progress_test.go`. Do not add a package, move wake presentation vocabulary into `internal/ops`, strengthen the documented `prompts -> ops` coupling, change progress decisions, or change lifecycle evidence.
validation: pre-commit run --files internal/agent/workdetection.go internal/agent/workdetection_test.go internal/prompts/wake.go internal/prompts/builder.go internal/prompts/builder_test.go internal/ops/integration_progress.go internal/ops/integration_progress_test.go

desc: Make integration-analysis phase-to-role-pair validation consume the package's existing canonical mapping.
done_when: `validateIntegrationAnalysisRolePair` in `internal/ops/submit_verdict.go` obtains the expected role pair from `analysisRolePair` or the existing `sliceIntegrationRolePair` and `globalIntegrationRolePair` constants instead of repeating both string literals. Slice and global tasks still accept their matching pair, reject the opposite pair with the same actionable task/phase/wanted/got information, and reject an invalid phase. `rg -n '"slice-integration-pair"|"integration-pair"' internal/ops --glob '!*_test.go'` reports the canonical definitions in `internal/ops/integration_reconcile.go` and no duplicate mapping in `submit_verdict.go`.
scope: Own `internal/ops/submit_verdict.go`, `internal/ops/submit_verdict_test.go`, `internal/ops/integration_reconcile.go`, and `internal/ops/integration_reconcile_test.go`. Do not change role-pair names, analysis phases, verdict authorization, reconciliation, or pipeline topology.

desc: Reconcile zero-slice and frozen-pipeline documentation with the implemented capability boundary.
done_when: ADR-0113's global-readiness and frozen-compatibility sections, `specs/protocols/task-lifecycle.md`'s lifecycle and persisted-evidence wording, and `support-docs/USAGE_MULTI_AGENTS.md`'s operator guidance all state the same boundary: coverage records and sliced-integration capability are required only when the frozen contributing cohort has at least two scopes; a zero- or one-scope cohort persists no coverage records and may proceed through an existing valid global integration pair; `pipeline_upgrade_required` applies when a qualifying cohort requires slice topology that the frozen pipeline lacks. The documents no longer imply that every incomplete legacy sliced topology blocks the direct-global bypass, and code/tests remain unchanged.
scope: Own only `specs/architecture/ADR/0113-sliced-integration-analysis-and-final-closure.md`, `specs/protocols/task-lifecycle.md`, and `support-docs/USAGE_MULTI_AGENTS.md`. Preserve the implemented progress decision, frozen-pipeline behavior, direct-global bypass, and all code and tests.
